Update. I am updating my CV right now.
Review. She is reviewing my cover letter.
Search. I am searching for internships every night.
Consider. I am considering two companies.
Compete. Two hundred students are competing for the same place.
Require. Every company requires English.
Upload. I am uploading my CV to their website.
Hey. What are you doing?
I am uploading documents. Again. This is the fourth time this week.
Fourth? Why?
Every company requires something different. One wants a photo, one does not.
I am preparing mine too. I am updating the CV right now, actually.
How many are you searching for?
Six this month. I am considering two seriously, and the rest are just practice.
Practice is smart. Two hundred people are competing for the one I want.
Two hundred? Are you still applying?
Of course. Someone has to be the one, and today I am feeling optimistic.
I’m preparing my CV this week.
I’m searching for an internship at the moment.
I’m considering two companies.
They’re not hiring right now.
And you? What are you working on?

Hi, sorry, I am recording this on the bus because I am going to an interview and I am already nervous. Anyway. I am doing something different this month. I am not applying to the big names anymore, because everybody applies there and nobody answers. I am searching for smaller companies instead, and guess what, two of them replied in three days. Three days. I am updating my CV for each one now, which takes forever, but it is working. What are you doing about yours right now? Tell me, because I need ideas.

Good afternoon and welcome back to the careers fair. I am standing in front of the biggest stand and the queue is getting longer every minute. They are not really talking to anybody, to be honest. They are just collecting CVs and saying thank you. Now, over on the left, something different is happening. The small companies are talking to every single student, and two of them are interviewing people on the spot, right here. So here is my advice: go to the small stands first. Nobody is waiting there. Back to you.
